title: The deepest cut
intro: Cut four equal squares of side x from the corners of a 30 cm × 30 cm sheet and fold the flaps up into an open box. Cut too little and the box is shallow; cut too much and the base shrinks to nothing. Somewhere between is the most volume you can get.
prompt: What cut depth x, in centimetres, maximises the volume?
debrief:
`V(x) = x(S - 2x)²` with S = 30. Differentiating and setting to zero gives a maximum at **x = S/6 = 5 cm**, where V = 5 × 20² = **2000 cm³**.

The answer worth keeping is not 5 — it is **S/6**. The optimum is a *ratio*, so it transfers to any square sheet you are ever handed, and that is the difference between solving this problem and memorising it.

Notice how the endpoints behave here, because it is the exact opposite of the detective in this pack. At x = 0 there is no height and the volume is zero; at x = 15 the base has vanished and the volume is zero again. Both boundaries are minima, so the interior stationary point genuinely is the answer — which is only knowable by *checking*, not by assuming. The same calculus, run on the same interval, can put the answer in the middle or at the edge; the procedure is what tells you which.
